newsitem.title: USA: D&P lowers Mercury senior debt to default.
newsitem.headline: D&P lowers Mercury senior debt to default.

text.p: Duff & Phelps Credit Rating Co said Monday it has downgraded Mercury Finance Co's senior debt to double-d, a default rating, from triple-C.
The commercial paper rating remains at D-five.
The rating action on the senior debt responds to Mercury's inability to pay $15 million of debt due last Friday, Duff & Phelps said.
Friday's debt represented the first medium-term notes to come due since the beleaguered auto finance company began defaulting on debt, Duff & Phelps analyst Tom Kmiotek said.
Mercury's woes began January 29 when it said it would have to lower its earnings over the last four years by about $90 million.

The cut in earnings was due to accounting discrepencies Mercury blamed on its controller, James Doyle. But a day later, Doyle's lawyer accused Mercury of a charade and said Doyle was cooperating with federal authorites.

Since then, Mercury has defaulted on millions of dollars in debt, been served with a search warrant by FBI agents seeking financial records, hired a turnaround and bankruptcy specialist as chief executive officer, and has been named a defendant in more than half a dozen lawsuits surrounding the misstated earnings.

The company also secured $50 million in short-term financing from the Bank of America on February 10. Mercury said it was negotiating with lenders Monday to secure the proper waivers to extend that loan through June 30.
